featured_reviews.name: Aryan Penikal
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are in South Bombay, you definitely have to give Flame-in-go a shot. The outlet is so underrated, it can easily be one of the go to affordable shawarma places in South Bombay. Their menu consists of a variety of products starting from Rs. 40 all the way to Rs. 200. You feel like having something light, there's a chicken sandwich or a shawarma pav for you. You feel to hungry they have chicken salads. You are in mood for a proper shawarma, you'll get that obviously.

Not just the variety of products but also the flavours. All their inventory items come in same flavours. From flavours like Tandoori and Cheeseburst and all the way to Mint mayo, Korean and Thai chilly, you'll get a lot of options. Their classic shawarma tastes equally good as well if you crave the OG.

They have definitely increased the standards for street food shops by maintaining proper hygiene and amazing customer service. Basically the Dev Momos of Shawarma vendors.

Sardar Pavbhaji, the oldest pav bhaji hotel in Tadeo, is a must-visit for all pav bhaji lovers. Known for their delicious pav bhaji, they serve up a perfect blend of quality and generous portions.

Food - 10/10
Service - 8/10
Ambiance - 9/10
VFM - 7/10
What stands out - Make your own Mexican food is one of a kind in Mumbai

Decided to try this newely opened place right opposite my house. The outlet is small but extremely well made. They have 2-3 tables but primarily this is a delivery kitchen. This is a one of kind make your own Mexican food restaurants. Its similar to make your own wok type of a restaurant but for Mexican food. Loved this concept. You can pick and choose from variety of ingreidients to go in your burrito / taco or salad. The pricing is something i found was slightly on a higher side considering its primarily into delivery. Make no mistake its totally worth it, but i just feel its still on a higher side.

The servers are pretty skilled and know what goes well with what. I got myself two burritos and loved it both. One was Fajita and other was chipotle paneer. The chipotle flavour is mild but along with all those salsa sauces, it tastes outstanding. The Fajita burrito was my favourite. They have four types of salsa sauces and all are amazing. They specialize in what is called California Mexican slightly different from Tex-Mex. California Mexican has a lot more chipotle flavour in it. We also tried their fresh lemonade and it is just amazing. Super refreshing.

All in all this is an outstanding new Mexican place. I am surely ordering from here again.

We noticed many varieties of cream puddings displayed, which looked very tempting. Since it was our first time, we asked the staff which one was the best, and they suggested the Seetha Phal (custard apple) cream pudding, so we ordered that along with rose milk falooda.
As they said, the Seetha Phal cream pudding was extraordinary and super in taste, very rich and satisfying. The rose milk falooda was good, but not as special as the pudding. They also serve many other juices, desserts, and snacks.
Prices are definitely on the higher side, and most items feel expensive. The ambience is simple and nothing fancy, and the service is just okay. Overall, the Seetha Phal cream pudding is highly recommended if you visit here.

A perennial favorite among locals and tourists alike, Haji Ali Juice Centre is an iconic culinary landmark nestled at the threshold of the historic Haji Ali Dargah. Since its inception in the 1960s, this bustling establishment has cultivated a legendary status, evolving from a modest stop for pilgrims into a vibrant gastronomic institution. It is celebrated for its unwavering commitment to quality, utilizing fresh, seasonal ingredients to craft an extensive repertoire of refreshments that have become synonymous with Mumbai's street food culture.
Reviewers frequently highlight the establishment's ability to maintain high standards of hygiene and flavor despite the immense daily crowds. The atmosphere is quintessentially Mumbai—a high-energy, casual setting where patrons often enjoy their treats standing on the pavement or from the comfort of their cars, adding a unique drive-in charm to the experience.
• Signature Fruit Creams: The "Sitaphal" (custard apple) cream is universally acclaimed as a must-try masterpiece, featuring a luscious, thick consistency generously laden with fresh fruit chunks.
• Exotic Shakes & Juices: Guests often praise the Mango Milkshake for its rich, creamy texture and the "Triveni"—a sophisticated blend of mango, strawberry, and kiwi juices.
• Savoury Accompaniments: Beyond beverages, the menu boasts popular fusion snacks like the Jain Pizza and the indulgent Cheese Toast, noted for its generous cheese-to-bread ratio.
• Late-Night Accessibility: Operating from the early morning until well past midnight, it serves as a reliable sanctuary for night revelers seeking high-quality refreshments.

featured_reviews.name: Sanoop ks
featured_reviews.review_text:
Haji Ali Juice Centre is one of those places in Mumbai that almost everyone has heard about, and naturally, expectations are quite high before visiting. The menu is extensive, filled with a wide variety of juices, shakes, and desserts that look appealing at first glance. The taste of the items is definitely good—fresh, flavorful, and satisfying to an extent. You can tell that the ingredients are of decent quality and prepared well.

However, beyond that initial impression, nothing truly stands out. There isn’t anything particularly unique or memorable about the flavors that would make you want to come back again and again. It feels like what you get is something you could easily find at many other juice shops across the city.

One of the biggest drawbacks is how overhyped the place feels. Because of its popularity and constant crowd, you go in expecting something exceptional, but the experience turns out to be fairly average. This mismatch between expectation and reality is quite noticeable.

On top of that, the pricing feels a bit on the higher side for what is offered. While the quality is decent, it doesn’t quite justify the cost, making it seem overrated.

Overall, Haji Ali Juice Centre delivers good taste but nothing extraordinary. It’s worth trying once for the experience, but it may not live up to the hype surrounding it.

Chung Fa Chinese Restaurant is a place I’ve visited a number of times over the past few years, and it has consistently delivered a satisfying Indo-Chinese dining experience in Mumbai.

On my most recent visit, we ordered the Chicken Manchow soup, chicken crispy, and fried wantons for starters.

The soup was flavourful and well-prepared, setting a good tone for the meal. The chicken crispy also stood out as one of the better dishes that was nicely done and enjoyable. The fried wantons, however, were just about average in comparison.

Overall, both the starters and the main dishes were tasty and met expectations.

The kitchen does take a bit of time with preparation, but the quality of the food makes the wait worthwhile.

Service has generally been good, attentive and efficient without being intrusive, which adds to the overall comfort of the dining experience.

One area where the restaurant is somewhat limited is desserts. The options are minimal, and typically consist of packaged ice cream cups rather than freshly prepared items.

All things considered, Chung Fa remains a dependable choice for Indo-Chinese cuisine in the Tardeo area. It’s a place I’ve enjoyed returning to over time, and one I would recommend for a satisfying and familiar dining experience.

Everything we ordered was super yummy, freshly cooked and light on tummy(not oily at all unlike other gujarati restaurants).

We ordered following items:
1. Panki with chutney - panki was nicely cooked and soft. Chutney was tasty and not too spicy thankfully.
2. Kand tikki chaat (purple yam chaat) - Recommended to me by their staff. Very very unique chat, you will surely not get the same thing elsewhere.
3. Undhiyo and bajra rotla - Undhiyo was tasty and fresh, not oily at all. Bajra rotla was surprisingly soft. Served with few pieces of amba halad, raw haldi, and jaggery.
4. Bajra kichu - Unique form of kichu and very healthy too for winter.
5. Masala tea - served with sesame crackers. Tea was great too. By the way they also didn't charge me milk for the baby , which was sweet.

I wish I had more appetite to try more items. I will come back next time for sure

PS: They have a washroom too which was clean.
Waiting time is around 20 minutes which was manageable. Their service was quite quick by the way.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flute 24 Hrs had a mixed dining experience overall.

The starters were quite good and flavourful. We ordered the Korean Style Chicken and Murgh Phoolzadi Kebab, both of which were enjoyable and well prepared.

However, the mains was a disappointment. We ordered the Murg Angara, and it lacked proper flavour and tasted quite off compared to the strong start from the appetizers. I also felt the recommendation for the mains could have been better.

Something unique about Flute in comparison to most other restaurants is that a 5% service fee is included and charged to the bill. This is interesting because tipping in India is optional as far as I am aware. This resulted in a modest increase in the bill of around ₹100 for the three dishes. However I would usually tip more but because the service fee was included it made little sense to top anything and felt somewhat redundant.

The service was nice as per my expectation but this practice is one which I have encountered in few restaurants and certainly is not a norm and so is something to be aware about.

The restaurant otherwise was good though but slightly priced on the premium side.

I thought some items were inappropriately priced. One small roti at ₹88 (excluding any taxes) seemed like a rip off because it averaged 3-4 rotis on just one dish so felt a bit unusual seeing ₹300 on a side dish of a basic small roti.

That said, the ambience was quite nice. The restaurant was air-conditioned, comfortable and relaxing, with an IPL match playing alongside mild instrumental music which made for a calm dining atmosphere.

Overall, good starters and ambience, but inconsistent mains and somewhat inflated pricing.

I recently visited Flute Restaurant inside Krishna Palace Hotel at Grant Road for lunch along with a colleague, and the experience was delightful from start to finish. The ambience is classy yet comfortable, with a touch of elegance that makes it perfect for both business and casual outings.

We started with Chicken Manchow Soup, Dynamite Prawns, and a refreshing Watermelon Salad, all of which set a great tone for the meal. The Mumbai Sunshine cocktail was vibrant and well-balanced.

For the mains, we had Chicken Lehsuni, Bhatti Da Murg, and Cheese Garlic Naan – the Lehsuni Chicken was undoubtedly the star of the show with its bold, garlicky taste. Mutton Rogan Josh also stood out with its rich spicy and aromatic flavour. The Chicken Biryani that followed was aromatic and satisfying.

Desserts were a highlight – the Butterscotch Ice Cream, Malai Kulfi, and the indulgent Pull Over Chocolate Cake were all top-notch, especially the chocolate cake, which was rich and gooey.

The service was attentive and prompt, complementing the excellent food. Overall, Flute Restaurant offers a well-rounded dining experience with great food, good service, and a pleasant setting. Definitely worth a visit if you're around Grant Road.

customer_updates.name: SMRUTISIKHA PRADHAN
customer_updates.text:
• Cannon Pav Bhaji is one of Mumbai's most famous street food destinations, located opposite CSMT.
• Established in 1975 by a former Indian Army veteran, it has been serving Mumbaikars and travelers for decades.
• Known for its rich, buttery, and flavorful pav bhaji made in the traditional Mumbai style.
• The pav is perfectly toasted with butter and pairs wonderfully with the delicious bhaji.
• The place has a unique old-Mumbai charm and is an important part of the city's food heritage.
• Despite being a simple standing food stall, it attracts food lovers from across India.
• Quick service, authentic taste, and a nostalgic atmosphere make the experience memorable.
• A must-visit spot for anyone who wants to enjoy Mumbai's legendary pav bhaji and experience a piece of the city's culinary history.

Overall: Great taste, rich history, and a true Mumbai street-food experience. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Pardeshi
featured_reviews.review_text: Canon Pav Bhaji did not live up to the hype at all. I have had much better pav bhaji at many other places. I ordered one Amul Butter Pav Bhaji and one Amul Butter Cheese Pav Bhaji. Both were extremely bland and lacked proper spices. There was an excessive amount of butter added, to the point that only butter’s taste was overpowering everything else—no real flavor of the bhaji could be felt. The pav bhaji was not even served properly hot, which made the experience worse. On top of that, the prices are very high for the quality and taste offered. This review is purely based on my personal experience, and unfortunately, it was very disappointing.

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Sonawane
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Cannon Pav Bhaji near CST and, unfortunately, the experience was quite disappointing. We tried several items Pav Bhaji, Sheera, Sabudana Khichdi and Lassi and to be frank, everything was absolutely tasteless. For a place that is always crowded and located in such a prime spot, I genuinely expected much better in terms of flavour and quality.

The Pav Bhaji lacked the rich, buttery taste and balanced spices that you normally find even at simple street side stalls across Mumbai. The Sheera was bland and lacked the aroma and sweetness that make it enjoyable. Sabudana Khichdi, which is usually comforting and flavourful, felt underwhelming as well. Even the Lassi didn’t have the freshness or thickness you would hope for.

It feels like the only advantage this place has is its central location right outside CST, which naturally attracts tourists and daily commuters. In contrast, some of the other nearby stalls actually serve tastier food at far more economical prices.

Overall, Cannon Pav Bhaji didn’t live up to its hype or its location. If you’re looking for flavourful, satisfying Mumbai street food, you’re better off exploring the smaller stalls around the area.

featured_reviews.name: Vainateya Sahasrabudhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre in Mumbai my grandfather used to take me to have pav bhaji 2000 to 2014. Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is a renowned destination for street food enthusiasts, serving mouth-watering pav bhaji that has captured the hearts of many. This iconic eatery has earned a reputation for its delicious food, prompt service, and cozy ambiance.

Ambiance
The ambiance at Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is warm and inviting, perfect for a quick bite or a casual meal with friends and family. The decor is minimal, but the vibrant atmosphere and aroma of freshly cooked food make up for it.

Menu and Offerings
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre's menu is centered around its signature dish, pav bhaji, which is a flavorful mix of vegetables cooked in a rich tomato-based gravy, served with soft, buttery pav bread. Some popular items on the menu include-
- *Pav Bhaji*: The star of the show, made with a medley of vegetables and spices, served with pav bread.
- *Special Pav Bhaji*: A variation of the classic dish, made with extra butter and spices.

Quality and Taste
The quality and taste of Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre's offerings are exceptional. The pav bhaji is cooked to perfection, with a rich, buttery flavor that's hard to resist. Customers rave about the delicious food, and many have returned for years, making it a testament to the eatery's consistency.

Service
The service at Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is prompt and efficient, ensuring that customers receive their orders quickly and without any hassle. The staff is friendly and courteous, adding to the overall positive experience.

Value for Money
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre offers excellent value for money, with prices starting from around ₹120-₹200 per person for a meal. Given the quality and quantity of food, it's a steal.

Tips
- Visit Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre during off-peak hours to avoid crowds.
- Try the special pav bhaji for an extra-rich flavor experience.
- Pair your pav bhaji with a buttermilk, lassi or cold drink for a refreshing contrast.

Online Ordering and Delivery
For those who prefer the convenience of home delivery, Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre offers online ordering through platforms like Justdial and Zomato. This allows customers to enjoy their favorite dishes from the comfort of their own homes.

Overall Experience
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is a must-visit destination for anyone looking to experience the best of Mumbai's street food scene. With its delicious pav bhaji, prompt service, and excellent value for money, it's a culinary gem that will leave you wanting more.

Rating: 4.5/5 stars.
